question: After the decode/protocol-error bug is fixed, should OpenClaw accept the additive Codex harness auth-bootstrap contract and success-gated Codex runtime/plugin config writes as the permanent fix for fresh macOS Codex onboarding?
rationale: The central bug fix is in the right owner boundary, but auth bootstrap ownership and setup persistence are compatibility-sensitive provider/plugin decisions that automation should not finalize alone.

options.title: Fix, refresh, then land
options.body: Exclude decode/protocol errors from reconciliation, update against current main, rerun exact-head macOS/Codex onboarding proof, and land if maintainers accept the auth-provider compatibility change.

options.title: Split the API seam
options.body: Separate the generic authBootstrap plugin API decision from the macOS onboarding repair if maintainers want a narrower emergency fix.

options.title: Pause this direction
options.body: Keep the linked issue open and pause the branch until maintainers decide the permanent Codex harness auth boundary.

recommendation.title: Fix, refresh, then land
recommendation.body: Exclude decode/protocol errors from reconciliation, update against current main, rerun exact-head macOS/Codex onboarding proof, and land if maintainers accept the auth-provider compatibility change.
